apps.localizedDescription:
UTM is a full featured virtual machine host for iOS. In short, it allows you to run Windows, Android, and more on your iPhone and iPad.
This version runs on all iOS 14+ devices but lacks JIT support and is slower than regular UTM.


More information at https://getutm.app/

Features:

• Emulate any Processor
30+ processors supported by qemu including x86_64, ARM64, and RISC-V
• Run any Operating System
Windows, Linux, and more natively and securely on iOS within an App
• Fast Emulation
Para-virtualization with SPICE and JIT compilation with TCG
• High Compatibility
iOS 14+ supported. Works on iPhone and iPad. No jailbreak needed
• Free and Open Source
UTM and its dependencies are all free and open source
• Easy to Use
Configure and customize your VM in a native UI

versions.localizedDescription:
## Highlights
* (macOS) **DirectX graphics support for Windows**: Modern accelerated graphics for Windows 11 is now available on UTM for the first time. The driver is still experimental and games compatibility is currently limited.
* **Vulkan 1.3 graphics support for Linux**: Vulkan 1.3 is now supported on Linux guests with VirtIO Venus drivers in Mesa. Additionally, OpenGL 4.1 is supported with the new Apple Core OpenGL backend (macOS only).
* **Snapshots**: Save your VM at any point and go back to it later from the new Snapshots tab. Works with QEMU VMs on macOS and iOS 26, and with Apple Virtualization VMs on macOS 27.
* (macOS) **Apple Virtualization on macOS 27**: Pass USB devices through to your VM, turn on Secure Boot for Linux, run a VM without saving changes, and let VMs talk to each other with new networking modes.
* (macOS) **Smoother displays**: VMs now follow your display's refresh rate, so motion is fluid at up to 120 Hz on ProMotion displays.
* **More reliable USB**: Fast external SSDs can now be shared with a VM, and disconnecting a drive no longer freezes UTM. On macOS, drives are safely unmounted before they are handed to a VM.
* (iOS) **Better touch controls**: Gestures respond immediately, with new middle-click and right-drag actions and a new drag-to-scroll touch mode.
* (iOS) **iPhone Duo**: Fold your iPhone Duo like a laptop, and the bottom half becomes a keyboard or touchpad for your VM.

## Notes
* Suspended VMs may not resume correctly after updating. We recommend shutting down all VMs before you update UTM.
* The minimum supported versions are now macOS 12 and iOS 15.
* (macOS) Check out [UTM Games Database](https://db.getutm.app/) to see and report game compatibility for the experimental 3D driver. Re-install the Windows guest tools to get the latest driver.
* We now have a [development blog](https://blog.getutm.app)! Follow us for in-depth technical deep dives such as how we brought DirectX to QEMU.
* (macOS) To use the new graphics driver for Windows 11, we recommend a fresh install because the driver is still experimental and its use could lead to instability in the system. During the install of the guest tools, you will be prompted to select the experimental graphics driver. If you wish to install the new driver on a system that already is running the older display only driver, you need to run the uninstall script provided on the guest tools install ISO first.
* (macOS) Apple CoreGL backend does not support Vulkan or DirectX.
* Linux desktop rendering in Vulkan does not work due to lack of support for indirect draws for geometry shaders. Please configure your guest to use the older VirGL Gallium driver.
* SCSI drives on ARM64 virtual machines now use a VirtIO SCSI controller. A VM with a SCSI drive that was suspended, or has a snapshot with saved state, from an earlier version cannot resume it: delete the saved state and start the VM again.

## Changes (v5.0.9)
* Fixed Windows games hanging at startup while compiling shaders, in-game videos stalling after the first frame, and a failed 3D command resetting the guest's display (#7984)
* Fixed X11 apps under Xwayland not displaying with Vulkan on Linux
* Updated the virglrenderer, MoltenVK and DXMT graphics backends
* Security: Fixed memory corruption issues that could allow a malicious guest to gain sandboxed code execution in the isolated rendering process (thanks Xusheng Li at Vector 35 Inc)
* Home: VM notes now render Markdown (#3547) (thanks @pingu-the-penguin)
* Home: Fixed the confirmation for Clone, Stop or Move not appearing the second time it was requested for the same VM (thanks @ianplusplus)
* Home: Fixed the screenshot in the VM details being covered by a flat color on iOS 26, macOS 26 and visionOS 26
* Home: The size shown in the VM details now updates after the settings are closed (#7923)
* Home: A VM on an external drive that is listed as unavailable now stays available after its .utm is opened again (#7762)
* Home: Fixed one unreadable saved entry making every VM lose its saved location, window state and external drives
* Config: SCSI drives on ARM64 virtual machines now use a VirtIO SCSI controller, so guests without an LSI driver such as Rocky Linux and RHEL can see them (#7712)
* Config: Fixed PowerPC VMs created with the default settings failing to start because of too many CPU cores
* Config: Fixed the default devices of the Heathrow PowerMac (g3beige) machine keeping the VM from starting (#7803)
* Config: Fixed the default configuration of the Sam460ex machine failing to start (#7603)
* Config: Fixed new PowerPC VMs such as pseries defaulting to a network card that the machine rejects (#7592)
* Config: Fixed saving a VM failing after adding a TPM on RISC-V and LoongArch
* Config: Fixed a crash opening the terminal window of a VM whose configuration has no terminal settings
* Config: Fixed the host port of port forwards being replaced by the guest port when migrating a UTM 3 configuration
* QEMU: Guests with a VirtIO GPU now use the host display's refresh rate instead of always 75 Hz (#7820) (thanks @dragoshont)
* QEMU: Fixed saving a VM state that takes longer than 10 seconds being reported as "Timed out waiting for RPC" (#8052)
* QEMU: Fixed networking and the guest agent stalling once QEMU holds about a thousand open files, such as with a busy shared directory or 3D acceleration (#7624)
* QEMU: Fixed the display modes missing from the Monitors control panel of Mac OS guests on the mac99 machine (thanks @giovariot)
* QEMU: Fixed sound in Mac OS 9 and a hang at startup in its sound driver (#8033)
* QEMU: Fixed Mac OS 9 restarting to a black screen (#7999)
* QEMU: Fixed sound crackling and dropping out while the host is busy
* QEMU: Fixed Windows showing "Display output is not active." for several seconds on every boot with GPU acceleration
* QEMU: Fixed wrong colors in Windows programs that run in exclusive fullscreen with a 10-bit display format

## Installation

* [iOS](https://docs.getutm.app/installation/ios/)
* [macOS](https://docs.getutm.app/installation/macos/)

| File | Description | Installation | JIT | Hypervisor | USB |
|------|------------|--------------|-----|-----------|-----|
| UTM.deb | Jailbroken iOS version | Open in Cydia, dpkg, or Sileo | Yes | Yes(1) | Yes |
| UTM.dmg | macOS version | Mounting and copying UTM.app to /Applications | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| UTM.ipa | Non-jailbroken iOS version (sideloading) | AltStore, etc (see guide) | Yes(2) | No | No |
| UTM-HV.ipa | Non-jailbroken iOS version (TrollStore) | TrollStore | Yes | Yes(1) | Yes |
| UTM-SE.ipa | Non-jailbroken iOS version (sideloading) | AltStore, enterprise signing, etc | No | No | No |
| UTM-Remote.ipa | Remote client | Any | No | No | No |

1. Hypervisor on iOS requires an M1 iPad or newer.
2. Enabling JIT may require a separate JIT enabler such as [Jitterbug][2] or Jitstreamer.

### Verification (macOS)

The macOS release (`UTM.dmg`) is notarized by Apple. To verify the download, run `xcrun stapler validate UTM.dmg`. To verify the install, run `spctl -a -vv /Applications/UTM.app` and check that it is notarized and signed by `Turing Software, LLC (WDNLXAD4W8)`. This needs a network connection, so it cannot run from a sandbox that blocks outgoing connections.

[1]: https://getutm.app/install/
[2]: https://github.com/osy/Jitterbug

apps.name: WQ Files
apps.localizedDescription:
@ipavault | WQ Files

WQ Files is a file browser, app data manager and cache cleaner for iOS 27. "WQ" stands for worse_query, the sandbox technique it is built on. It reaches other apps' and system containers with no jailbreak and no kernel exploit. 

Requires: iOS 27, or iOS 26.0 – 26.7.2 (preliminary support). Tested on iOS 27.0.1, 27.2.1, 26.7.1, and 27.3 beta
Tools:

Apps: every app with its data size. Back up an app's data, restore the latest backup, clear its data (Documents, Library, tmp), open its folder, or share a backup as a ZIP over AirDrop, Files, Mail and so on.
Cache Cleaner: cache and temp size per app, with search, Select All / None / Large Caches (50 MB+) and crash logs. Long-press an app to jump to its Caches, tmp or data folder.
Files: browse, read and share files; each opens in the fitting tool, and Open As switches between them. Saving writes back in place (same inode, owner and attributes). Create folders, import files, rename and delete. Long-press a folder to share it as a ZIP.
Plist editor: browse dictionaries and arrays, edit values by type (switches for booleans, numbers, text, dates, data as hex), add, delete, rename and reorder. Saves in the file's own format (binary or XML).
Hex viewer and editor: any file size (read in pages), go to offset, find hex bytes or text, overwrite bytes in place. Changed bytes are highlighted until saved; the file size never changes.
Text and images: text is editable, images render, plists can also be edited as XML text.
Log: everything the app changed, plus the App Group it received.
⚠️ App Groups entitlement required
